A ray diagram illustrating the laws of reflection. A horizontal line represents a plane mirror with diagonal hash marks on the bottom side to show the non-reflective back. A dashed vertical line marks the Normal. An incident ray (solid line with an inward arrow) strikes the mirror at the base of the normal. A reflected ray (solid line with an outward arrow) leaves the same point. The angle between the incident ray and the normal is labelled 'i'. The angle between the reflected ray and the normal is labelled 'r'. The angle between the incident ray and the mirror surface is labelled 'g' (glancing angle). Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

Ray diagram for a convex mirror. An upright arrow (object) is placed in front of a convex mirror. A ray parallel to the principal axis reflects outwards, diverging as if originating from the virtual focus (F) behind the mirror. Another ray directed towards the centre of curvature (C) reflects back on itself. The virtual dashed extensions of these rays intersect behind the mirror between the pole and F, forming a small, erect, virtual image arrow. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

Cross-section of a simple periscope. A tall 'Z'-shaped or rectangular vertical tube with two open horizontal viewing windows. Two plane mirrors are placed at the internal corners, parallel to each other and inclined at 45 degrees to the vertical walls. A horizontal light ray from an object enters the top window, strikes the top mirror, reflects 90 degrees straight down, strikes the bottom mirror, and reflects 90 degrees horizontally out to a drawn eye. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.
